title: Forklift truck approval, types and designated locations practice questions
description: Practice questions on approved trucks, modifications, the eleven truck designations and where each may be used under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(a) to (e).

questions.question: Under 1910.178(a)(2), which powered industrial trucks shall meet the design and construction requirements of ANSI B56.1-1969 (Part II)?

options.A: Only trucks that will be used outdoors
options.B: All new powered industrial trucks acquired and used by an employer, except vehicles intended primarily for earth moving or over-the-road hauling
options.C: Only trucks operated on more than one shift a day
options.D: Only used trucks bought from a dealer

questions.explanation: "All new powered industrial trucks acquired and used by an employer shall meet the design and construction requirements for powered industrial trucks established in the" ANSI B56.1-1969 standard, "except for vehicles intended primarily for earth moving or over-the-road hauling."

questions.question: How does 1910.178(a)(3) say an approved truck shows that the testing laboratory approved it?

options.A: With a letter kept in the employer's files
options.B: With a sticker the employer prints after operator training
options.C: Only through the dealer's sales invoice
options.D: By bearing a label or some other identifying mark indicating approval by the testing laboratory

questions.explanation: "Approved trucks shall bear a label or some other identifying mark indicating approval by the testing laboratory."

questions.question: A user wants to make an addition to a truck that affects its capacity and safe operation. What does 1910.178(a)(4) require before the customer or user performs it?

options.A: The manufacturer's prior written approval
options.B: Approval from the local fire marshal
options.C: A verbal OK from the truck's regular operator
options.D: Notice to OSHA after the work is done

questions.explanation: "Modifications and additions which affect capacity and safe operation shall not be performed by the customer or user without manufacturers prior written approval."

options.A: The truck's designation letters
options.B: The dates on each operator's certification
options.C: Capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals
options.D: The hazard classification of the location where the truck works

questions.explanation: "Capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals shall be changed accordingly."

questions.question: What does 1910.178(b) set out "for the purpose of this standard"?

options.A: Eleven different designations of industrial trucks or tractors: D, DS, DY, E, ES, EE, EX, G, GS, LP, and LPS
options.B: Four lifting-capacity ratings that the manufacturer marks on each truck
options.C: Three hazard ratings that the employer assigns to each operator
options.D: Two categories of trucks: indoor trucks and outdoor trucks

questions.explanation: "For the purpose of this standard there are eleven different designations of industrial trucks or tractors as follows: D, DS, DY, E, ES, EE, EX, G, GS, LP, and LPS."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: For the purpose of this standard there are eleven different designations of industrial trucks or tractors as follows: D, DS, DY, E, ES, EE, EX, G, GS, LP, and LPS.

questions.question: A diesel powered unit has all the safeguards of the DS units, has no electrical equipment including the ignition, and is equipped with temperature limitation features. Which designation is it?

options.A: D
options.B: DS
options.C: DY
options.D: GS

questions.explanation: "The DY designated units are diesel powered units that have all the safeguards of the DS units and in addition do not have any electrical equipment including the ignition and are equipped with temperature limitation features."

questions.question: What sets the EX designated units apart from the E, ES, or EE units under 1910.178(b)(7)?

options.A: They are diesel powered and have no ignition system
options.B: Their electrical fittings and equipment are so designed, constructed and assembled that the units may be used in certain atmospheres containing flammable vapors or dusts
options.C: They are gasoline powered with minimum acceptable safeguards against inherent fire hazards
options.D: They use liquefied petroleum gas for fuel instead of gasoline

questions.explanation: EX units "differ from the E, ES, or EE units in that the electrical fittings and equipment are so designed, constructed and assembled that the units may be used in certain atmospheres containing flammable vapors or dusts."

questions.question: An electrically powered unit has, in addition to all of the requirements for the E and ES units, the electric motors and all other electrical equipment completely enclosed. Which designation is it?

options.A: E
options.B: ES
options.C: LPS
options.D: EE

questions.explanation: "The EE designated units are electrically powered units that have, in addition to all of the requirements for the E and ES units, the electric motors and all other electrical equipment completely enclosed."

questions.question: Under 1910.178(b)(12), what shall have been done before industrial trucks are considered for use in an atmosphere or location?

options.A: Every truck in the fleet shall have been converted to LP-gas
options.B: Travel lanes shall have been painted on the floor
options.C: The atmosphere or location shall have been classified as to whether it is hazardous or nonhazardous
options.D: Positive-pressure ventilation shall have been installed in the location

questions.explanation: "The atmosphere or location shall have been classified as to whether it is hazardous or nonhazardous prior to the consideration of industrial trucks being used therein".

questions.question: The trucks specified for each location in 1910.178(c)(2) are the minimum types required. What does 1910.178(c)(1) say about a truck having greater safeguards?

options.A: Industrial trucks having greater safeguards may be used if desired
options.B: Only the exact type listed for the location may be used
options.C: A truck with greater safeguards needs OSHA's written permission
options.D: Trucks with greater safeguards may be used only in unclassified locations

questions.explanation: "The industrial trucks specified under subparagraph (2) of this paragraph are the minimum types required but industrial trucks having greater safeguards may be used if desired."

questions.question: An atmosphere contains a hazardous concentration of hydrogen. Which power-operated industrial truck does 1910.178(c)(2)(i) allow there?

options.A: An approved truck designated as EX
options.B: A truck designated as DY
options.C: A truck designated as LPS
options.D: None; power-operated industrial trucks shall not be used in such atmospheres

questions.explanation: Paragraph (c)(2)(i) states: "Power-operated industrial trucks shall not be used in atmospheres containing hazardous concentration of acetylene, butadiene, ethylene oxide, hydrogen"; it names no designation that may be used there.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Gasoline vapors in quantities sufficient to produce explosive or ignitable mixtures exist intermittently under normal operating conditions. Which trucks does 1910.178(c)(2)(iii) permit there?

options.A: Any approved truck designated as Type D, E, G, or LP
options.B: Only approved power-operated industrial trucks designated as EX
options.C: Approved trucks designated as DS, ES, GS, or LPS
options.D: Gasoline powered G trucks only

questions.explanation: "Only approved power-operated industrial trucks designated as EX may be used" in atmospheres containing gasoline and the other listed gases or vapors where such concentrations "exist continuously, intermittently or periodically under normal operating conditions".

questions.question: 1910.178(c)(2)(iv) includes locations adjacent to Class I, Division 1 locations to which hazardous concentrations of gases or vapors might occasionally be communicated. Which "unless" condition does it state?

options.A: Unless such communication is prevented by adequate positive-pressure ventilation from a source of clear air, and effective safeguards against ventilation failure are provided
options.B: Unless the adjacent location is used only on weekends
options.C: Unless every truck there is fitted with an overhead guard
options.D: Unless a fire extinguisher is mounted on each truck

questions.explanation: Such locations are ones "to which hazardous concentrations of gases or vapors might occasionally be communicated unless such communication is prevented by adequate positive-pressure ventilation from a source of clear air, and effective safeguards against ventilation failure are provided."

questions.question: Under 1910.178(c)(2)(v), locations used for the storage of hazardous liquids or of liquified or compressed gases in sealed containers would not normally be considered hazardous unless what?

options.A: Unless the containers are stacked more than two high
options.B: Unless subject to other hazardous conditions also
options.C: Unless the storage is outdoors
options.D: Unless the containers are made of metal

questions.explanation: "Locations used for the storage of hazardous liquids or of liquified or compressed gases in sealed containers would not normally be considered hazardous unless subject to other hazardous conditions also."

questions.question: In atmospheres where dust of magnesium, aluminum or aluminum bronze may be present, what does 1910.178(c)(2)(ii)(b) require for a truck's fuses, switches, motor controllers, and circuit breakers?

options.A: Removal from the truck before it enters the area
options.B: A coat of nonconductive paint
options.C: Replacement after each shift in the area
options.D: Enclosures specifically approved for such locations

questions.explanation: "In atmospheres where dust of magnesium, aluminum or aluminum bronze may be present, fuses, switches, motor controllers, and circuit breakers of trucks shall have enclosures specifically approved for such locations."

questions.question: Which area does 1910.178(c)(2)(vi)(b) name as usually included in the EX classification?

options.A: All-metal dust and stock collectors vented to the outside
options.B: Coal pulverizing plants where the pulverizing equipment is essentially dust tight
options.C: The working areas of grain handling and storage plants
options.D: Areas where metal powders are stored in tight containers

questions.explanation: "The EX classification usually includes the working areas of grain handling and storage plants". The paragraph excepts "all-metal collectors vented to the outside", coal pulverizing plants "where the pulverizing equipment is essentially dust tight" and metal dusts and powders stored "in tight containers".

questions.question: A truck designated as E has been used in a location where easily ignitable fibers are stored, but not processed or manufactured. What does 1910.178(c)(2)(ix) say about that truck?

options.A: It shall be replaced with an EX truck at once
options.B: It shall be converted to LP-gas fuel
options.C: It may be used only outside the storage area
options.D: It may be continued in use

questions.explanation: In those locations, "Industrial trucks designated as E, which have been previously used in these locations may be continued in use."

questions.question: A storage warehouse is not classified as hazardous. Which statement matches what 1910.178(c)(2)(xi) says may be used there?

options.A: Any approved power-operated industrial truck designated as Type D, E, G, or LP, or trucks which conform to the requirements for these types
options.B: Approved EX trucks and no other type
options.C: DY, EE, or EX trucks and no other type
options.D: No power-operated industrial truck of any type

questions.explanation: "If not classified as hazardous, any approved power-operated industrial truck designated as Type D, E, G, or LP may be used, or trucks which conform to the requirements for these types may be used."

questions.question: A truck originally approved for gasoline fuel is converted to liquefied petroleum gas fuel in accordance with paragraph (q). Where does 1910.178(d) say it may be used?

options.A: Only where EX trucks are specified
options.B: Only on piers and wharves handling general cargo
options.C: In those locations where G, GS or LP, and LPS designated trucks have been specified
options.D: Nowhere, because a converted truck loses its approval

questions.explanation: Such trucks, "when converted to the use of liquefied petroleum gas fuel in accordance with paragraph (q) of this section, may be used in those locations where G, GS or LP, and LPS designated trucks have been specified in the preceding paragraphs."

options.C: A roll-down side curtain
options.D: A rear-view camera
